title: Regression Testing and Change Safety
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its role in reliable software.
Identify the topic in code or a realistic scenario.
Trace behavior and describe the expected result.
Apply the concept and verify it using a suitable test.

understand.concept: Regression testing reruns tests that protect previously working behavior after a change. Changes can introduce regressions through shared state, dependencies, altered interfaces, configuration, or unexpected side effects. Regression suites may include unit, integration, and end-to-end tests selected by risk and scope.
understand.whyItMatters: A fix or feature can break unrelated behavior. Regression checks provide evidence that the change did not reintroduce known defects or damage existing contracts.
understand.analogy: A careful process uses defined expectations, evidence, and repeatable checks to reduce uncertainty.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies software quality; the actual techniques depend on project context, tools, architecture, and risk.

explain.narrative: Record the defect or requirement, add a test when practical, make the change, rerun the focused test, then run the relevant regression suite. Review the diff and verify adjacent behaviors, configuration, and user-visible outcomes. Do not equate a small diff with low risk.

commonMistakes: Testing only the newly changed line.
Removing a failing test instead of investigating it.
Skipping regression checks because a diff is small.
Assuming a passing build guarantees user behavior remains correct.
